Introduction In this article, I’m going to discuss about Colpitts Oscillator. We will first look into the theory on how colpitts oscillator work and then implement one on our own in breadboard. We’ll also look into practical challenges of making the oscillator in a breadboard.
What’s a Oscillator? Oscillator is a circuit that generates a aleternating current signal from the power supplied to it without any external signal. This is generally used in generating a clock signal. It is also used in many sensing applications.
Any osillator circuit will generally have a amplifier, positive feedback and frequency determining components
In this article, we will look into a LC Oscillator circuit, namely Colpitts Osillator
Colpitts Oscillator As the name suggest, LC Tank circuit in positive feedback is the basic pronciple behind colputs oscillator. It uses capacitve voltage divider as its feedback source. The circuit diagram of Colpitts Oscillator with Op-amp is shown below.
This circuit can be divided into 3 parts:

Data Communication Data transfers can happen either serially or parallely. In serial communication,data bits are transmitted one by one whereas in parallel commuication, all bits are transmitted simultaneously.
Serial Communication can be asynchronous or synchronous. In asynchronous serial communication, a single byte is transferred at a time. It does not require a clock signal. Eg: UART In Synchronous coommunication,a block of data is transferred at a time. It requires a clock signal. Eg: I2C, SPI
Some Terms Simplex Data is transmitted only in one direction.
Duplex Data can be transmitted and received
Half Duplex Data is transmitted in both direction but only one eay at a time
Full Duplex Data is transmitted in both direction at the same time

contents:
UART is a two wired Asynchronous serial communication protocol
For UART Communication, we need to configure both devices with same speeed, i.e. baud rate.
Baud Rate is the data transfer rate on bits per sec.
UART Protocol requires a start bit and a stop bit. Data length can vary froom 5 bits to 9 bits. These should be configured before using UART. It uses NRZ (Non Return to zero) encoding for transmission. UART uses little endian bit ordering, which means the least significant bit is transmitted first.
